newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares rebound, seen down on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares rebound, seen down on Thursday.

text.p: Polish shares rose on Wednesday after a two-day fall but analysts said stronger post-price- fixing selling signalled a fall on Thursday and that there may not be enough positive factors to fuel significant growth.

"We'll likely have a slight fall at least on Thursday and then some growth soon, but it's hard to say if we'll beat our recent (14,282-point) high due to a lack of market-moving factors," said Tomasz Zalecki of Magnus brokerage.
Some analysts said significant growth was not likely next week because investors would not buy, as they might have last week, before news of possible interest rate changes abroad.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose one percent to 13,779.6 and turnover inched up 1.1 percent to 84.6 million zlotys ($30.9 million) on both markets. Gainers led losers by 50 to 15 with 12 stocks flat. Last week the market rose 9.3 percent in turnovers around 110 million zlotys each session.
Analysts said news such as firms' better July earnings also helped spur buying last week but that such possible positive signals would be lacking until mid-September.

Pawel Tarnowski of Raiffeisen Capital and Investment said construction firm Exbud, up by the daily maximum 10 percent, may have been helped by Monday's news that only 36.5 percent of the first leg of the firm's current rights issue was sold.
Analysts said the stock could also be buoyed by the firm's reiteration on Wednesday that it would invest 100 million zlotys ($36.5 million) over the next two years.

No stocks traded in continuous trade where mass privatisation NFI units closed at 86 zlotys ($31.4) in 0.3-million-zloty ($0.1 million) trade. In the regular bourse session they closed down 1.1 percent to 87 zlotys ($31.8) in 13-million-zloty ($4.8 million) trade.
